memory_candidates: Before dispatching proof work that CONSTRUCTS an inhabitant of a formalized structure, gate on the type being inhabited. Task 517 Phases 20 and 21 both spent dispatches against TPrime, which was provably empty at every 𝒯; a one-lemma inhabitedness check would have caught it at a fraction of the cost.

In a Lean transcription of a labelled/annotated deduction system, a clause quantified type-wide over labels where the source quantifies over the structure's domain will typically make the structure type UNINHABITED (via a containment field like Graph.edge_mem or Context.ctxSubset plus a coinfiniteness/freshness reserve), not merely too strong. The emptiness is silent until something tries to construct an inhabitant.

When a PDF's text layer is OCR-damaged, the damage is not uniform: Simpson1994's inference-rule FIGURES render as noise (`%(M) %(/\El)`) while surrounding prose extracts cleanly. Rule shapes — where cross-label vs label-local structure lives — are exactly what is lost. Read rule figures from the page raster, never the text layer.

A premise-free derivation at an arbitrary label (e.g. `impI`+`assumption` giving `x : A ⊃ A`) is a powerful probe for over-strong closure clauses in a proof-theoretic formalization: it instantiates the clause at every label at once.
